claims.text: Magnetic field-induced directional solidification at 10 T followed by aging at 500°C for 10 hours will improve the strength of CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed treatment will improve the ductility of CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed treatment will improve the fracture resistance of CoCrFeMnNi.
Magnetic field-induced directional solidification will create an aligned columnar grain structure in CoCrFeMnNi.
Aging CoCrFeMnNi at 500°C for 10 hours will precipitate coherent nanoparticles.
The applied magnetic field will induce crystallographic texture during directional solidification.
The aging treatment will produce precipitation hardening.
The coherent nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion.
The aligned grain structure and coherent nanoparticles will cause the predicted improvements in strength, ductility, and fracture resistance.
The directional-solidification rate will be 10 mm/s.
The aging treatment will be conducted under vacuum.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement depends on optimization of magnetic-field strength and aging conditions.
Non-uniform grain structure or precipitation may occur and may adversely affect the alloy's mechanical properties.
CoCrFeMnNi processed without magnetic field-induced directional solidification and aging is the proposed experimental control.
The hypothesis is falsified if the untreated control exhibits similar or better tensile strength, ductility, and fracture resistance.
